text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II

  

    List - I

    List - II

  

  

    A.

    Planck's constant

    I.

    $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}$

  

  

    B.

    Stopping potential

    II.

    $\mathrm{T}^{-1}$

  

  

    C.

    Work function

    III.

    $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}$

  

  

    D.

    Threshold frequency

    IV.

    $\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-1}$

  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the dimensions of Planck's Constant (h)

According to the photon energy equation $\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{h}ν$, where E is energy and $ν$ is frequency.

Planck's constant is given by $\mathrm{h}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{v}}$

The dimensions of energy (E) are $[\mathrm{E}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$.

The dimensions of frequency ( $v$ ) are $[v]=\left [\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$.

Therefore, dimensions of h :

$[\mathrm{h}]=\frac{\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{T}^{-1}]}=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$

Thus, A → III

For the dimensions of stopping potential ( $\mathrm{V}_{0}$ )

Stopping potential is defined as the potential difference required to stop the fastest moving electrons. The work done by the potential is equal to the kinetic energy, $\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{qV}_{0}$, where q is charge.

So, stopping potential is $\mathrm{V}_{0}=\frac{\mathrm{w}}{\mathrm{q}}$.

The dimensions of work ( W ) are $[\mathrm{W}]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$.

The dimensions of charge ( $\mathrm{q}=\mathrm{I}\times \mathrm{t}$ ) are $[\mathrm{q}]=[\mathrm{AT}]$.

Therefore, dimensions of stopping potential is:

$[\mathrm{V}_{0}]=\frac{\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{AT}]}=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-3}\mathrm{A}^{-1}\right ]$

Thus, $\mathrm{B}\to$ IV.

For the dimensions of work function ( $𝜙$ )

The work function is the minimum energy required to eject an electron from a metal surface. Since it is a form of energy, its dimensions are the same as energy (E).

So, the dimensions of work function is $[𝜙]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$

Thus, $\mathrm{C}\to \mathrm{I}$.

For the dimensions of threshold frequency ( $v_{0}$ )

Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of incident radiation required for photoelectric emission.

Frequency is defined as the reciprocal of the time period $\left (v=\frac{1}{\mathrm{T}}\right )$.

So, the dimensions of threshold frequency is $[v_{0}]=\left [\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$

Thus, $\mathrm{D}\to$ II.

Therefore, the correct match is A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: Two cars $A$ and $B$ are moving in the same direction along a straight line with speeds $100\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$ and $80\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$, respectively such that car $A$ is moving ahead of car $B$. A person in car $B$ throws a stone with a speed $v$ so that it hits the car $A$ with a speed of $5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The value of $v$ is $____$ $\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{h}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $v_{A}=100\text{km h}^{-1}$ and $v_{B}=80\text{km h}^{-1}$ in the same direction, with A ahead of B. The stone is thrown with speed $v$ relative to car B and hits car A with speed $5\text{m s}^{-1}$ relative to car A.

Converting, $5\text{m s}^{-1}=5\times \dfrac{18}{5}=18\text{km h}^{-1}$.

Velocity of the stone relative to the ground:

$v_{S}=v_{B}+v=80+v$

Velocity of the stone relative to car A:

$v_{S}-v_{A}=(80+v)-100=v-20$

Setting this equal to $18\text{km h}^{-1}$:

$v-20=18\Rightarrow v=38\text{km h}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: At $t=0$, a body of mass 100 g starts moving under the influence of a force $(5\hat{\mathrm{i}}+10\hat{\mathrm{j}})\mathrm{N}\cdot$ After 2 s its position is $(2x\hat{\mathrm{i}}+5y\hat{\mathrm{j}})\mathrm{m}$. The ratio $x:y$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mass of the body, $\mathrm{m}=100\mathrm{g}=0.1\mathrm{kg}$

The constant force acting on the body, $⃗{F}=(5\hat{ı}+10\hat{ȷ})N$

The time interval of motion, $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$

As the body started from rest, so the initial velocity at $\mathrm{t}=0,\vec{\mathrm{u}}=0$

The position at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s},\vec{\mathrm{r}}=(2\mathrm{xi}+5\mathrm{y})\mathrm{j})\mathrm{m}$

According to Newton's Second Law of Motion :

$\vec{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{a}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\vec{\mathrm{F}}}{\mathrm{m}}$

Substituting the values :

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{5\hat{ı}+10\hat{ȷ}}{0.1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{a}}=(50\hat{ı}+100\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

From the second equation of motion for constant acceleration:

$\vec{\mathrm{s}}=\vec{\mathrm{ut}}+\frac{1}{2}\vec{\mathrm{a}}t^{2}$

Since $\vec{\mathrm{u}}=0$ :

$\vec{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{1}{2}\vec{\mathrm{a}}\mathrm{t}^{2}$

Substituting the acceleration and time :

$\vec{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{1}{2}(50\hat{ı}+100\hat{ȷ})(2)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{1}{2}(50\hat{ı}+100\hat{ȷ})(4)$

$\Rightarrow$ $⃗{s}=2(50\hat{ı}+100\hat{ȷ})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{s}}=(100i\hat{ı}+200\hat{ȷ})\mathrm{m}$

On comparing the calculated displacement with the given position $(2x\hat{i}+5y\hat{j})$ :

For the x -component: $2\mathrm{x}=100\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=50$

For the $y$-component: $5y=200\Rightarrow y=40$

So, the required ratio is,

$\frac{x}{y}=\frac{50}{40}=5:4$

Therefore, the ratio $\mathrm{x}:\mathrm{y}$ is $5:4$. 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text: If $x$ and $y$ coordinates of a projectile as a function of time $(t)$ are given as $24t$ and $43.6t-4.9t^{2}$, respectively, then the angle (in degrees) made by the projectile with horizontal when $t=2\mathrm{s}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Horizontal position of projectile is given as $\mathrm{x}=24\mathrm{t}$

Vertical position of projectile is given as $\mathrm{y}=43.6\mathrm{t}-4.9\mathrm{t}^{2}$

Velocity is the rate of change of position with respect to time $\left (⃗{V}=\frac{d⃗{r}}{dt}\right )$.


[IMG]


For the velocity component along horizontal, $(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}})$ :

$v_{x}=\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(24t)=24\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

The horizontal velocity remains constant throughout the motion.

For the velocity component along vertical, $(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}})$ :

$v_{y}=\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left (43.6t-4.9t^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}=43.6-(2\times 4.9)\mathrm{t}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{y}=43.6-9.8t$

So, the velocities at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ is,

$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}=24\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}=43.6-9.8(2)=43.6-19.6=24\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

The angle $θ$ that the velocity vector makes with the horizontal is given by

$\tan θ=\frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{y}}}{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{x}}}$

Substituting the values calculated for $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ :

$\tan θ=\frac{24}{24}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\tan θ=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ=45^{\circ }$

Therefore, the angle made by the projectile with the horizontal at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ is $45^{\circ }$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
The height in terms of radius of the earth $(R)$, at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\frac{g}{9}$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface, is

$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Newton's Law of universal gravitation, the acceleration due to gravity ( $g$ ) on the surface of Earth is,

$g=\frac{GM}{R^{2}}\ldots \text{(i)}$


[IMG]


Where $G$ is the gravitational constant, $M$ is the mass of the Earth, and $R$ is the radius of the Earth.

If the body is placed at a height h above the Earth's surface, its total distance from the centre of the Earth becomes $(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h})$. The acceleration due to gravity at this height is:

$\mathrm{g}^{'}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h})^{2}}......(ii)$

Dividing equation (ii) by equation (i) :

$\frac{\mathrm{g}^{'}}{\mathrm{g}}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}/(\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h})^{2}}{\mathrm{GM}/\mathrm{R}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{g^{'}}{g}=\frac{R^{2}}{(R+h)^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{g}^{'}=\mathrm{g}\left (\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}}\right )^{2}$

It is given that the acceleration due to gravity at height h is $\mathrm{g}^{'}=\frac{\mathrm{g}}{9}$ :

$\frac{g}{9}=g\left (\frac{R}{R+h}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{9}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}+\mathrm{h}=3\mathrm{R}\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}=2\mathrm{R}$

Therefore, the height at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\frac{g}{9}$ is $2R$. 

Thus, the correct option is (C).

text: A metal string $A$ is suspended from a rigid support and its free end is attached to a block of mass $M$. Second block having mass 2 M is suspended at the bottom of the first block using a string $B$. The area of cross sections of strings $A$ and $B$ are same. The ratio of lengths of strings of $A$ to B is 2 and the ratio of their Young's moduli $(Y_{A}/Y_{B})$ is 0.5 . The ratio of elongations in $A$ to $B$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Young's Modulus (Y) is defined as the ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain :

$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{A}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}/\mathrm{L}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{L}=\frac{\mathrm{FL}}{\mathrm{AY}}\ldots (ii)$

Where, F is the tension in the string, L is the original length, A is the area of cross-section. Y is the Young's Modulus.


[IMG]


For string B

This string supports only the bottom block of mass 2 M .

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}=2\mathrm{Mg}$

For string A

This string supports both mass M and the mass 2 M hanging below it.

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{A}}=\mathrm{Mg}+2\mathrm{Mg}=3\mathrm{Mg}$

The ratio of lengths is $\frac{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=2$

The ratio of Young's moduli is $\frac{\mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{Y}_{\mathrm{B}}}=0.5$.

The areas are same, $A_{A}=A_{B}=A$.

Using the formula of extension in string (i),

$\frac{\Delta L_{A}}{\Delta L_{B}}=\frac{F_{A}L_{A}/A_{A}Y_{A}}{F_{B}L_{B}/A_{B}Y_{B}}=\left (\frac{F_{A}}{F_{B}}\right )\times \left (\frac{L_{A}}{L_{B}}\right )\left (\frac{Y_{B}}{Y_{A}}\right )$

Substituting the values :

$\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left (\frac{3\mathrm{Mg}}{2\mathrm{Mg}}\right )\times (2)\times \left (\frac{1}{0.5}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left (\frac{3}{2}\right )\times 2\times 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\Delta \mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{B}}}=3\times 2=6$

Therefore, the ratio of elongations in A to B is 6. 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text: A water spray gun is attached to a hose of cross sectional area $30\mathrm{cm}^{2}$. The gun comprises of 10 perforations each of cross sectional area of $15\mathrm{mm}^{2}$. If the water flows in the hose with the speed of $50\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$, calculate the speed at which the water flows out from each perforation. (Neglect any edge effects)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an incompressible fluid, the volume of fluid entering a pipe per unit time must equal the volume of fluid leaving the pipe per unit time.

Volume Flow Rate (In) = Volume Flow Rate (Out)

$A_{1}v_{1}=A_{2}v_{2}$

Where A is the area and v is the velocity of the fluid.

The area of hose is $\mathrm{A}_{1}=30\mathrm{cm}^{2}=30\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

The speed in hose is $\mathrm{v}_{1}=50\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}=0.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

Number of perforations is $\mathrm{n}=10$.

The area of one perforation is $\mathrm{a}=15\mathrm{mm}^{2}=15\times \left (10^{-3}\mathrm{m}\right )^{2}=15\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

So, total area of exit is, $\mathrm{A}_{2}=\mathrm{n}\times \mathrm{a}=10\times 15\times 10^{-6}=150\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Using the equation of continuity:

$A_{1}v_{1}=A_{2}v_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2}=\frac{A_{1}v_{1}}{A_{2}}$

Substituting the values :

$v_{2}=\frac{\left (30\times 10^{-4}\right )\times 0.5}{150\times 10^{-6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{2}=\frac{15\times 10^{-4}}{150\times 10^{-6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}_{2}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the speed at which the water flows out from each perforation is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : If the average kinetic energy of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ molecules, kept in two different sized containers are same, then their temperatures will be same.

Reason R : The r.m.s speed of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ molecules are same at same temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$
A is true but $𝐑$ is false
A is false but $𝐑$ is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the kinetic theory of gases, the average translational kinetic energy ( $\mathrm{K}_{\text{avg}}$ ) of a gas molecule is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (T).

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{3}{2}\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{T}$

Where $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the Boltzmann constant.

So, the average kinetic energy depends only on the temperature and not on the mass of the molecule or the size/volume of the container.

Since $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{avg}}$ is the same for both $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}_{2}$, their temperatures (T) must be identical.

Therefore, Assertion A is true.

The root mean square (r. m. s.) speed ( $\mathrm{v}_{\text{rms}}$ ) of a gas molecule is given by the formula:

$v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$

Where R is the universal gas constant, T is the absolute temperature, and M is the molar mass of the gas.

At the same temperature (T), $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{rms}}$ is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass (M).

Since the molar mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}(2\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol})$ is different from $\mathrm{O}_{2}(32\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol})$, their r.m.s. speeds will be different even at the same temperature.

Therefore, Reason R is false.

Hence, Assertion A is true, but Reason R is false. 

So, the correct option is (C).

text:
The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $α$ is increased from $T_{1}$ to $T_{2}$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta L_{1}$. The temperature is further increased from $T_{2}$ to $T_{3}$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_{2}$.

Given $T_{3}+T_{1}=2T_{2}$ and $T_{2}-T_{1}=\Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_{2}$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a metal of length $L$ having coefficient of linear expansion $α$ is heated by temperature $\Delta T$, then the change in length is given as $\Delta \mathrm{L}=\mathrm{L}α\Delta \mathrm{T}$

For the first interval of heating $(\mathrm{T}_{1}\to \mathrm{T}_{2})$ :

The increase in length $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}$ is given by $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}=\mathrm{L}_{1}α(\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1})$

It is given that $\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\Delta \mathrm{T}$ :

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}=\mathrm{L}_{1}α\Delta \mathrm{T}.....(i)$

The new length at temperature $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ is:

$\mathrm{L}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{1}+\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}=\mathrm{L}_{1}(1+α\Delta \mathrm{T})........(ii)$

For the second interval of heating, ( $\mathrm{T}_{2}\to \mathrm{T}_{3}$ )

The increase in length $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}$ depends on the length at the start of this stage $(\mathrm{L}_{2})$ :

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{2}α(\mathrm{T}_{3}-\mathrm{T}_{2})$

From the given condition $\mathrm{T}_{3}+\mathrm{T}_{1}=2\mathrm{T}_{2}$ :

$\mathrm{T}_{3}-\mathrm{T}_{2}=\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}$

Since $\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\Delta \mathrm{T}$, then $\mathrm{T}_{3}-\mathrm{T}_{2}=\Delta \mathrm{T}$.

Substituting this into the $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}$ formula:

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=\mathrm{L}_{2}α\Delta \mathrm{T}.......(iii)$

Substitute the value of $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ from equation (ii) into equation (iii) :

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=[\mathrm{L}_{1}(1+α\Delta \mathrm{T})]α\Delta \mathrm{T}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=(\mathrm{L}_{1}α\Delta \mathrm{T})(1+α\Delta \mathrm{T})$

From equation (i), we know $\mathrm{L}_{1}α\Delta \mathrm{T}=\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}$.

$\Delta \mathrm{L}_{2}=\Delta \mathrm{L}_{1}(1+α\Delta \mathrm{T})$

Therefore, the value of $\Delta L_{2}$ is $\Delta L_{1}[1+α\Delta T]$. 

Thus, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
A uniform disc of radius $R$ and mass $M$ is free to oscillate about the axis $A$ as shown in the figure. For small oscillations the time period is $____$ .

(g is acceleration due to gravity)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The axis through A is the tangent to the disc lying in its plane, so the disc swings out of its plane as a physical pendulum with its centre of mass at distance $d=R$ from the axis.

By the perpendicular axis theorem, the moment of inertia of a uniform disc about a diameter is $I_{d}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2}\right )=\dfrac{1}{4}MR^{2}$.


[IMG]

The tangent at A is parallel to a diameter at distance $R$, so by the parallel axis theorem

$I_{A}=\dfrac{1}{4}MR^{2}+MR^{2}=\dfrac{5}{4}MR^{2}$

For a small angular displacement $θ$, the restoring torque is $τ=-MgRθ$, so

$T=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{I_{A}}{MgR}}=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{\frac{5}{4}MR^{2}}{MgR}}=2π\sqrt{\dfrac{5R}{4g}}$

The value $\dfrac{3}{2}MR^{2}$ belongs to a tangent axis perpendicular to the plane of the disc, which is not the axis shown.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: A rigid dipole undergoes a simple harmonic motion about its centre in the presence of an electric field $\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{1}=\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{x}$. If another electric field $\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{2}=2\mathrm{E}_{0}(\hat{y}+\hat{z})$ is introduced to the system, what will be the percentage change in the frequency of the oscillation (approximate)?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a dipole with dipole moment $\vec{\mathrm{p}}$ is placed in an electric field $\vec{\mathrm{E}}$, the restoring torque is $⃗{τ}=-\vec{\mathrm{p}}\times \vec{\mathrm{E}}$

The magnitude of restoring torque is $τ=-\mathrm{pE}\sin θ$.

For small $θ$,

$τ\approx -\text{pEθ}$

The equation of motion is $\mathrm{I}\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}θ}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=-\mathrm{pE}θ$, where I is the moment of inertia.

The angular frequency is $ω=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{pE}}{\mathrm{I}}}$, so the frequency f is:

$f=\frac{ω}{2π}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{f}=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{pE}}{\mathrm{I}}}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}\propto \sqrt{\mathrm{E}}$

Where E is the magnitude of the net electric field.

Initial electric field is $\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{1}=\mathrm{E}_{0}\widehat{\mathrm{x}}$.

Magnitude of initial electric field is $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{E}_{0}$.

The additional electric field is $\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{2}=2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{y}}+2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{z}}$.

So, the net electric field is

$\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{\mathrm{net}}=\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{1}+\vec{\mathrm{E}}_{2}=\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{x}}+2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{y}}+2\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{\mathrm{z}}$

Magnitude of the net electric field is,

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{net}}=\sqrt{(\mathrm{E}_{0})^{2}+(2\mathrm{E}_{0})^{2}+(2\mathrm{E}_{0})^{2}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{E}_{0}^{2}+4\mathrm{E}_{0}^{2}+4\mathrm{E}_{0}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{net}}=\sqrt{9\mathrm{E}_{0}^{2}}=3\mathrm{E}_{0}$

Let $f_{1}$ be the initial frequency and $f_{2}$ be the final frequency.

$\frac{\mathrm{f}_{2}}{\mathrm{f}_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{3\mathrm{E}_{0}}{\mathrm{E}_{0}}}=\sqrt{3}\approx 1.732$

So, the percentage change is

$\Delta %=\left (\frac{\mathrm{f}_{2}-\mathrm{f}_{1}}{\mathrm{f}_{1}}\right )\times 100$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta %=(\sqrt{3}-1)\times 100$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta %=(1.732-1)\times 100=0.732\times 100=73.2%$

Therefore, the approximate percentage change in the frequency of oscillation is $73%$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

From the circuit given below, the capacitance between terminals $A$ and $B$ shown in the circuit is $____$ $μ\mathrm{F}$.

(take $C_{1}=C_{2}=C_{3}=1μ\mathrm{F}$ and $C_{4}=2μ\mathrm{F}$.)

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the node between $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ be X ,


[IMG]


The wire (short circuit) connects terminal A to the node between $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{3}$. Thus, this node is at the same potential as A.

So, capacitor $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ is connected between A and X .

The capacitor $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ is connected between A and X .

The capacitor $C_{3}$ is connected between $A$ and $B$.

The capacitor $\mathrm{C}_{4}$ is connected between X and B .

So, the simplified circuit is,


[IMG]


Given values of capacitances are, $\mathrm{C}_{1}=1μ\mathrm{F},\mathrm{C}_{2}=1μ\mathrm{F},\mathrm{C}_{3}=1μ\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{4}=2μ\mathrm{F}$

Both $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ are connected between point A and point X in parallel.

The equivalent capacitance $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{AX}}$ is :

$C_{AX}=C_{1}+C_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $C_{AX}=1μF+1μF=2μF$

Now, the combination $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{AX}}$ is in series with $\mathrm{C}_{4}$ because the charge must flow through $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{AX}}$ to reach $\mathrm{C}_{4}$. So, the equivalent capacitance ( $\mathrm{C}^{'}$ ) is

$\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}^{'}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{AX}}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}_{4}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\mathrm{C}^{'}}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C}^{'}=1μ\mathrm{F}$

The entire top branch ( $C^{'}$ ) is now in parallel with $C_{3}$, as both are connected across the main terminals $A$ and $B$.

The total equivalent capacitance $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is :

$C_{\mathrm{eq}}=C^{'}+C_{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{eq}}=1μ\mathrm{F}+1μ\mathrm{F}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{eq}}=2μ\mathrm{F}$

Therefore, the equivalent capacitance between A and B is $2μ\mathrm{F}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason $𝐑$

Assertion A : In electrostatics, a conductor does not store any net charge inside.

Reason R : Inside the capacitor (with no dielectric medium), the free charge carriers, if placed between the plates of capacitor, experience force and drift.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$
A is true but $𝐑$ is false
A is false but $𝐑$ is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside a conductor is zero $(\mathrm{E}=0)$.

According to Gauss's Law $\left (\int \mathrm{E}\cdot \mathrm{dA}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\text{in}}}{𝜖_{0}}\right )$, if the electric field is zero everywhere inside, the net charge enclosed ( $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{in}}$ ) by any Gaussian surface inside the conductor must also be zero. Therefore, any excess charge resides entirely on the outer surface.

Therefore, assertion A is true.

Inside a charged capacitor, there is a uniform electric field between the plates.


[IMG]


If free charge carriers (like electrons or ions) are placed in this region, they will experience an electric force ( $\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{qE}$ ). This force causes the charges to accelerate or drift toward the plate of opposite polarity.

Therefore, reason R is true.

While both statements are scientifically true, reason R describes the behaviour of charges in an external field between two conductors (the plates). It does not explain why the net charge inside a solid conductor is zero (which is due to mutual repulsion and the resulting zero internal field).

So, both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A . 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text:
A solenoid has a core made of material with relative permeability 400 . The magnetic field produced in the interior of solenoid is 1.0 T . The magnetic intensity in SI units is $α\times 10^{5}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

(Free space permeability $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}$ SI units.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The relative permeability of the core is $μ_{\mathrm{r}}=400$.

The magnetic field applied is, $\mathrm{B}=1.0\mathrm{T}$.

The permeability of free space is $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{T}\cdot \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{A}$.

The magnetic induction $B$ in a material is related to the magnetic intensity $H$ by the total permeability of the medium ( $μ$ ) :

$\mathrm{B}=μ\mathrm{H}\ldots \text{(i)}$

The total permeability $μ$ is the product of the permeability of free space and the relative permeability of the material :

$μ=μ_{0}μ_{r}$

Substituting this into the first equation :

$\mathrm{B}=μ_{0}μ_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{H}$

$\RightarrowH=\frac{B}{μ_{0}μ_{r}}$

Substituting the given values,

$H=\frac{1.0}{\left (4π\times 10^{-7}\right )\times 400}$

$\Rightarrow$ $H=\frac{1}{1600π\times 10^{-7}}$

$\RightarrowH=\frac{1}{16π}\times 10^{5}=a\times 10^{5}\Rightarrow α=\frac{1}{16π}$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is $\frac{1}{16π}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (B).

text: A magnetic field vector in an electromagnetic wave is represented by $⃗{B}=B_{0}\sin \left (2πvt-\frac{2πx}{λ}\right )\hat{j}$. Its associated electric field vector is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The argument of the sine function is $\left (2πvt-\frac{2πx}{λ}\right )$. This indicates the wave is propagating along the positive x -axis.

Let the unit vector for the direction of propagation be $\hat{\mathrm{n}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}$.


[IMG]


In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field vector $(\vec{\mathrm{E}})$, the magnetic field vector $(\vec{\mathrm{B}})$, and the direction of propagation ( $\widehat{\mathrm{n}}$ ) are mutually perpendicular. Their relationship is given by:

$\widehat{\mathrm{E}}=\widehat{\mathrm{B}}\times \widehat{\mathrm{n}}$

It is given that $\vec{\mathrm{B}}$ is along $\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ :

$\widehat{\mathrm{E}}=\hat{ȷ}\times \hat{ı}=-\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

The magnitude of the electric field and magnetic field in a vacuum are related by the speed of light (c):

$\mathrm{E}_{0}=\mathrm{cB}_{0}$

The speed of light is the product of frequency and wavelength: $\mathrm{c}=νλ$.

$\mathrm{E}_{0}=vλ\mathrm{B}_{0}$

The electric field must have the same phase as the magnetic field. So, the electric field component is,

$\vec{\mathrm{E}}=\mathrm{E}_{0}\sin \left (2πv\mathrm{t}-\frac{2π\mathrm{x}}{λ}\right )(-\widehat{\mathrm{k}})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{E}}=-vλ\mathrm{B}_{0}\sin \left (2πv\mathrm{t}-\frac{2π\mathrm{x}}{λ}\right )\hat{\mathrm{k}}$

Therefore, the associated electric field vector is $-vλ\mathrm{B}_{0}\sin \left (2πv\mathrm{t}-\frac{2π\mathrm{x}}{λ}\right )\hat{\mathrm{k}}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text: A convex lens is made from glass material having refractive index of 1.4 with same radius of curvature on both sides. The ratio of its focal length and radius of curvature is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a thin lens with two curved surfaces, the focal length ( $f$ ) is related to the refractive index ( $n$ ) and the radii of curvature $(\mathrm{R}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{R}_{2})$ by Lens Makers' formula,


[IMG]


$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(\mathrm{n}-1)\left (\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{1}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}\right )$

The refractive index of the material, $\mathrm{n}=1.4$.

The lens is convex with the same radius of curvature on both sides (R).

According to the Cartesian sign convention:

The first surface is convex towards the incident light, so $\mathrm{R}_{1}=+\mathrm{R}$.

The second surface is concave towards the incident light, so $R_{2}=-R$.

Substituting the values into the formula :

$\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(1.4-1)\left (\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}-\frac{1}{-\mathrm{R}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=(0.4)\left (\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=0.4\times \frac{2}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{0.8}{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{f}=\frac{\mathrm{R}}{0.8}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{f}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{1}{0.8}=1.25$

Therefore, the ratio of its focal length and radius of curvature is 1.25 . 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text: An unpolarized light of certain intensity passes through a combination of two polarizers whose transmission axes are at $30^{\circ }$ and $90^{\circ }$, respectively, with respect to the horizontal axis. A third polarizer with its transmission axis at $60^{\circ }$ with the horizontal axis is placed between the two existing polarizers. The ratio of the output intensities with and without the third polarizer is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When polarized light of intensity $\mathrm{I}_{\text{in}}$ passes through a polarizer, the intensity of the transmitted light $\left (\mathrm{I}_{\text{out}}\right )$ is given by Malus's Law

$I_{\text{out}}=I_{\text{in}}\cos ^{2}θ$

Where $θ$ is the angle between the polarization direction of the incident light and the transmission axis of the polarizer.

The initial intensity of unpolarised light $=\mathrm{I}_{0}$.

After the first polarizer (at $30^{\circ }$ ), the light becomes polarized with intensity $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I}_{0}$.

This light then hits the second polarizer (at $90^{\circ }$ ). The angle between them is $θ=90^{\circ }-30^{\circ }=60^{\circ }$.

So, the final intensity without third polarizer is,

$I_{\text{without}}=I_{2}=I_{1}\cos ^{2}60^{\circ }=\left (\frac{1}{2}I_{0}\right )\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}I_{0}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{I_{0}}{8}$

The intensity after the first polarizer (at $30^{\circ }$ ) is $\mathrm{I}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{I}_{0}$.

This light hits the middle polarizer (at $60^{\circ }$ ). The angle is $θ_{12}=60^{\circ }-30^{\circ }=30^{\circ }$.

So, intensity after middle polarizer $(\mathrm{I}_{3})$ :

$I_{3}=I_{1}\cos ^{2}30^{\circ }=\left (\frac{1}{2}I_{0}\right )\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{1}{2}I_{0}\times \frac{3}{4}=\frac{3I_{0}}{8}$

This light hits the final polarizer (at $90^{\circ }$ ). The angle is $θ_{23}=90^{\circ }-60^{\circ }=30^{\circ }$.

So, final intensity after the final polarizer is

$\mathrm{I}_{\text{with}}=\mathrm{I}_{3}\cos ^{2}30^{\circ }=\left (\frac{3\mathrm{I}_{0}}{8}\right )\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )^{2}=\frac{3\mathrm{I}_{0}}{8}\times \frac{3}{4}=\frac{9\mathrm{I}_{0}}{32}$

So, the ratio of the output intensities with and without the third polarizer is,

$\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\text{with}}}{\mathrm{I}_{\text{without}}}=\frac{\left (\frac{9\mathrm{I}0}{32}\right )}{\left (\frac{\mathrm{I}0}{8}\right )}=\frac{9}{4}$

Therefore, the ratio of the output intensities with and without the third polarizer is $9/4$. 

Thus, the correct option is (C).

text:
In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, only a few alpha particles rebound back because

A. The size of gold nucleus is very small as compared to the size of gold atom.

B. Alpha particle and gold nucleus have equal charge.

C. The impact parameter is minimum for a few alpha particles.

D. A few alpha particles have very high kinetic energy.

E. Only a few alpha particles undergo head-on collision with the nuclei.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the experiment, alpha particles (positively charged helium nuclei) are fired at a thin gold foil. Rutherford observed that most particles passed straight through, but a tiny fraction (about 1 in 8000 ) reflected back at angles greater than $90^{\circ }$.


[IMG]


Statement A: Rutherford concluded that the positive charge and most of the mass of the atom are concentrated in an extremely small region called the nucleus. Since the nucleus is tiny compared to the total volume of the atom, the probability of an alpha particle hitting it or coming close enough to be repelled backward is very low.

Hence, statement A is true.

Statement B: Alpha particles have a charge of +2 e , while a gold nucleus has a charge of +79 e . They do not have equal charges. Hence, statement B is false.

Statement C: The impact parameter (b) is the perpendicular distance of the initial velocity vector of the alpha particle from the centre of the nucleus.


[IMG]


A rebound or large-angle scattering occurs when the impact parameter is very small (close to zero), meaning the particle is heading almost directly toward the nucleus. Only a few particles have such a small impact parameter. Hence, the statement C is true.

Statement D: The kinetic energy of the incident alpha particles is generally uniform in the beam; high kinetic energy would actually make it easier to penetrate closer to the nucleus rather than causing the few rebounds mentioned. Hence, the statement D is false.

Statement E: A head-on collision occurs when the particle moves directly toward the centre of the nucleus $(\mathrm{b}=0)$. Because the nucleus is so small, only a very small number of particles are aligned for such a collision. Hence, the statement E is true.

Therefore, statements A, C, and E are the correct reasons for the observed phenomenon. 

Thus, the correct option is (D).

text: The de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated through a potential difference V is $λ_{\mathrm{e}}$ and the de Broglie wavelength associated with a proton accelerated through the same potential difference is $λ_{\mathrm{p}}$. If their corresponding masses are $m_{\mathrm{e}}$ and $m_{\mathrm{p}}$, respectively, then the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths $\left (\frac{λ_{e}}{λ_{p}}\right )$ is $____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to de Broglie's hypothesis, the wavelength associated with a particle of momentum p is:

$λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}$

Where h is Planck's constant.

Kinetic energy is given by $\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}$.

In terms of linear momentum, the kinetic energy can be written as

$K=\frac{m^{2}v^{2}}{2m}=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$

Thus, momentum $\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{mK}}$.

When a particle of charge q is accelerated through a potential difference V , the work done on it becomes its kinetic energy:

$\mathrm{K}=\mathrm{qV}$

Substituting this into the momentum equation:

$\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{mqV}}$

So, the de-Broglie's wavelength is $λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{mqV}}}$

The charge on electron is $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{e}}=\mathrm{e}$, so the wavelength for an electron is $λ_{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{eV}}}$

The charge on proton is $\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{p}}=\mathrm{e}$, so the wavelength for a proton is $λ_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}\mathrm{eV}}}$

Taking the ratio $\frac{λ_{\mathrm{e}}}{λ_{\mathrm{p}}}$ :

$\frac{λ_{\mathrm{e}}}{λ_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}/\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{eV}}}{\mathrm{h}/\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}\mathrm{eV}}}=\frac{\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}\mathrm{eV}}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}\mathrm{eV}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{λ_{\mathrm{e}}}{λ_{\mathrm{p}}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}}$

Therefore, the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths is $\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}}$. 

Thus, the correct option is (A).

text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason $𝐑$

Assertion A : A diode under reverse-biased condition provides very small current which is nearly independent of voltage until a critical limit at which the current increases drastically.

Reason R : Below the critical voltage limit, only majority charge carriers flow which increases drastically above critical voltage.

choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$
A is true but $𝐑$ is false
A is false but $𝐑$ is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In reverse bias the p-side is connected to the negative terminal and the n-side to the positive terminal, so the majority carriers are pulled away from the junction and the depletion layer widens.

Only minority carriers (electrons in the p-region, holes in the n-region) drift across the junction. Their number is fixed mainly by temperature, so the reverse current is very small (of the order of $μ\text{A}$) and nearly independent of the applied voltage.

At a critical reverse voltage, the breakdown voltage, the reverse current increases sharply. Hence Assertion A is true.

Below the breakdown voltage the current is carried by minority carriers, not majority carriers, so Reason R is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A diode has Zener voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.5 W , then the minimum resistance to be used in series with this diode for safety when it is connected to a 25 V power supply is $____$ $\Omega$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In breakdown the voltage across the Zener diode stays at $V_{Z}=10\text{V}$, so the maximum safe current is

$I_{\max }=\dfrac{P_{\max }}{V_{Z}}=\dfrac{0.5}{10}=0.05\text{A}$

The series resistor takes the rest of the supply voltage, $V_{R}=25-10=15\text{V}$, and carries the same current as the diode.

The current must not exceed $I_{\max }$, so

$R_{\min }=\dfrac{V_{R}}{I_{\max }}=\dfrac{15}{0.05}=300\Omega$

Hence, the answer is 300.

text:
A gun mounted on the ground fires bullets in all directions with same speed. The farthest distance the bullets could reach is 6.4 m . The speed of the bullets from the gun is $____$ $\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.

$\text{(take}\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\text{)}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A bullet fired with an initial velocity $u$ at an angle $θ$ with the horizontal. On resolving the initial velocity of bullet.


[IMG]


Horizontal component: $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{u}\cos θ$

Vertical component: $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{u}\sin θ$

The time of flight $(T)$ is the time taken for the bullet to return to the ground $(y=0)$.

Using the equation $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{y}}\mathrm{t}-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{gt}^{2}$ :

$0=(\mathrm{u}\sin θ)\mathrm{T}-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{gT}^{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=\frac{2\mathrm{u}\sin θ}{\mathrm{g}}$

The horizontal range $(\mathrm{R})$ is the distance covered during this time :

$\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{x}}\times \mathrm{T}=(\mathrm{u}\cos θ)\left (\frac{2\mathrm{u}\sin θ}{\mathrm{g}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin (2θ)}{\mathrm{g}}$

The range is maximum when $\sin (2θ)$ is maximum. The maximum value of the sine function is 1 (which occurs when $2θ=90^{\circ }\Rightarrow θ=45^{\circ }$ ).

So, the maximum horizontal range is

$\mathrm{R}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}}{\mathrm{g}}$

The maximum horizontal range is given as 6.4 m

$6.4=\frac{u^{2}}{10}\Rightarrow u^{2}=64\Rightarrow u=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the speed of the bullets from the gun is $8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. 

Hence, the correct answer is 8 .

text:
Two identical small bar magnets each of dipole moment $3\sqrt{5}\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{T}$ are placed at a center to center separation of 10 cm , with their axes perpendicular to each other as shown in figure. The value of magnetic field at the point P midway between the magnets is $α\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{T}$. The value of $α$ is $____$

$\left (μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{Tm}/\mathrm{A}\right )$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each magnet has $M=3\sqrt{5}\text{J T}^{-1}$, and P is $r=5\text{cm}=0.05\text{m}$ from each centre, so $r^{3}=1.25\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{3}$.

P lies on the axis of the horizontal magnet, so its field at P is the axial field:

$B_{1}=\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{2M}{r^{3}}=\frac{10^{-7}\times 6\sqrt{5}}{1.25\times 10^{-4}}=\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{1.25}\times 10^{-3}\text{T}$

P lies on the equatorial line of the vertical magnet, so its field at P is the equatorial field:

$B_{2}=\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\frac{M}{r^{3}}=\frac{10^{-7}\times 3\sqrt{5}}{1.25\times 10^{-4}}=\frac{3\sqrt{5}}{1.25}\times 10^{-3}\text{T}$

$B_{1}$ is along the axis of the horizontal magnet and $B_{2}$ is antiparallel to the moment of the vertical magnet, so the two fields are perpendicular:

$B=\sqrt{B_{1}^{2}+B_{2}^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{1.25}\times 10^{-3}\sqrt{6^{2}+3^{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}\times 3\sqrt{5}}{1.25}\times 10^{-3}=\frac{15}{1.25}\times 10^{-3}=12\times 10^{-3}\text{T}$

Comparing with $α\times 10^{-3}\text{T}$ gives $α=12$.

Hence, the answer is 12.

text:
A circular coil of radius 2 cm and 125 turns carries a current of 1 A . The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.4 T . The axis of the coil makes an angle of $30^{\circ }$ with the direction of the magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil is $α\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{N}.\mathrm{m}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ .

$(π=3.14)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The magnetic dipole moment of a single loop of wire carrying current I and enclosing area A is given by

$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{IA}$


[IMG]


For a coil consisting of N turns, the total magnetic moment is :

$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{NIA}$

Since the coil is circular with radius r , the area A is $π\mathrm{r}^{2}$.

$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{NI}\left (π\mathrm{r}^{2}\right )$

The torque experienced by a magnetic dipole in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{\mathrm{B}}$ is given by the vector cross product :

$⃗{τ}=\vec{\mathrm{m}}\times \vec{\mathrm{B}}$

The magnitude of this torque is :

$τ=\mathrm{mB}\sin θ$

Where $θ$ is the angle between the magnetic moment (which is along the axis of the coil) and the magnetic field direction.

The number of turns is $\mathrm{N}=125$.

The current in the coil is $\mathrm{I}=1\mathrm{A}$.

The radius of circular coil is $\mathrm{r}=2\mathrm{cm}=0.02\mathrm{m}$.

The magnitude of magnetic field strength is, $\mathrm{B}=0.4\mathrm{T}$.

The angle between the magnetic field and magnetic moment is $θ=30^{\circ }$.

Substituting the values into the torque formula:

$τ=\left (\mathrm{NI}π\mathrm{r}^{2}\right )\mathrm{B}\sin θ$

$\Rightarrow$ $τ=\left (125\times 1\times 3.14\times (0.02)^{2}\right )\times 0.4\times \sin 30^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $τ=(125\times 3.14\times 0.0004)\times 0.4\times 0.5$

$\Rightarrow$ $τ=314\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{N}.\mathrm{m}=α\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{N}\cdot \mathrm{m}\Rightarrow α=314$

Therefore, the value of a is 314 .

text:
In a double slit experiment, when one of the slits is covered by a transparent mica sheet of refractive index 1.56 , the central fringe shifts to the position of $7^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe, obtained with both slits uncovered. If the light source wavelength is 450 nm , the thickness of mica sheet is $α\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}$. The value of $α$ is

$____$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a transparent sheet of thickness t and refractive index $μ$ is placed in the path of one of the beams, the light travels a distance $t$ in the medium instead of air.

The optical path length in the sheet is $μ\mathrm{t}$.

The extra path difference introduced ( $\Delta \mathrm{p}$ ) is:

$\Delta \mathrm{p}=μ\mathrm{t}-\mathrm{t}=(μ-1)\mathrm{t}$

A bright fringe occurs when the path difference is an integer multiple of the wavelength $(λ)$ :

$\Delta \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{m}λ$

Where m is the order of the fringe.

Since the central fringe (where path difference was zero) shifts to the position of the 7th bright fringe ( $\mathrm{m}=7$ ), the introduced path difference must be equal to $7λ$ :

$(μ-1)\mathrm{t}=7λ$
